Task 1: Perform an Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)¶

Objective: Analyse the Global AI & Data Jobs Salary Dataset to discover trends, patterns, and relationships among variables using statistical summaries and graphical representations.

# Distribution of the numerical features
numerical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns.tolist()
n_cols = 4
n_rows = math.ceil(len(numerical_cols) / n_cols)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, n_cols, figsize=(20, n_rows * 4))
axes = axes.flatten()

for i, col in enumerate(numerical_cols):
    sns.histplot(df[col], kde=True, ax=axes[i], color='skyblue', bins=30)
    axes[i].set_title(f'Distribution of {col}', fontsize=10)
    axes[i].set_xlabel('')
    axes[i].set_ylabel('')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
In [22]:
# Distribution of the categorical features
categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns.tolist()
n_cols = 4
n_rows = math.ceil(len(categorical_cols) / n_cols)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, n_cols, figsize=(20, n_rows * 4))
axes = axes.flatten()

for i, col in enumerate(categorical_cols):
    top_10 = df[col].value_counts().nlargest(10).index
    sns.countplot(data=df[df[col].isin(top_10)], y=col, ax=axes[i], order=top_10)
    axes[i].set_title(f'Top 10: {col}', fontsize=10)
    axes[i].set_xlabel('Count')
    axes[i].set_ylabel('')
    
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Relationship of categorical features with salary_usd
target = 'salary_usd'
fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, n_cols, figsize=(20, n_rows * 5))
axes = axes.flatten()

for i, col in enumerate(categorical_cols):
    top_10 = df[col].value_counts().nlargest(10).index
    sns.boxplot(data=df[df[col].isin(top_10)], x=target, y=col, ax=axes[i], order=top_10)
    axes[i].set_title(f'{target} by {col} (Top 10)', fontsize=10)
    axes[i].set_xlabel('')
    axes[i].set_ylabel('')
    axes[i].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=90)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

In [24]:
# Select only numerical features for correlation matrix
numerical_df = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number])
corr_matrix = numerical_df.corr()

# Plot the heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 12))
sns.heatmap(corr_matrix, annot=True, fmt='.2f', cmap='coolwarm', linewidths=0.5, cbar_kws={'shrink': 0.8})
plt.title('Correlation Matrix of Numerical Features', fontsize=16)
plt.show()

From EDA, we can see that there are no significant outliers in the target and model features, with a single high cardinality categorical feature 'country', however, we can see that the target salary_usd is highly correlated and inversely correlated with certain features such as experience_years, salary_usd, bonus_usd, layoff_risk, and employee_satisfaction. Most of them are acceptable to be kept in model training as it makes logical sense on how it affect the target, with the exception of bonus_usd, which is likely entirely based on salarry_usd which leads to data leakage.

Task 2¶

In this section, we will use PyCaret to build an end-to-end ML pipeline. Since salary_usd is a continuous variable, this is a Regression problem.

In [25]:
from pycaret.regression import *
import mlflow

# Connect to Mlflow server
mlflow.set_tracking_uri("http://127.0.0.1:5000")

# Initialize PyCaret Setup
reg_setup = setup(
    data=df,
    target='salary_usd',
    session_id=123, # Replicable session
    normalize=True, # Scaling and normalization
    normalize_method='minmax', # MinMax scaling
    transformation=True, # Transform features to be normally distributed
    transform_target=True, # Transform the target variable
    ignore_features=['bonus_usd'], # Remove possible data leakage features from model
    log_experiment=True,
    experiment_name='ai_salary_prediction',
    log_plots=True,
    memory=False
)
